History of Present Illness:
44-year-old woman. Fourteen hours of persistent right upper abdominal pain after a meal, with nausea and vomiting. Prior brief episodes resolved within an hour; this episode has not.

Physical Examination:
Right upper-quadrant tenderness and inspiratory arrest during deep subcostal palpation; no generalized guarding. Temperature 37.4 C; heart rate 88/min; BP 116/70 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; SpO2 97% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 11.8 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.1 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 220 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 136 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.8 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 45 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 32 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 48 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 43 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 85 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)
Serum pregnancy test: negative (reference negative)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: gallstones, impacted gallbladder-neck stone, wall thickness 5 mm, pericholecystic fluid and focal probe tenderness. Common bile duct 4 mm.
